title: A Compass for the Ledger
premise: In 1748 Trieste, apprentice clockmaker Ivo Marchetti is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a stranger, Lena Kovač, waiting with letters in the unmistakable hand of her father—a man officially dead for six years. The handwriting proves he faked his death to escape a merchant house that stole his shipping ledger, the true record of debts and inheritances owed to dozens of families, including Ivo's own late mother. Hunted by the house's enforcers as the harbor clock ticks toward a dawn tide, Ivo and Lena must copy and notarize the ledger's pages into official hands before the ship carrying the victors' historians sails away with the sanitized version of history. They succeed at cost: the master clock is destroyed in the struggle, Ivo abandons his apprenticeship to become the ledger's public keeper, and Lena boards the ship alone—not fleeing, but to confront the living father she no longer recognizes.
about_author: Ada Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging maritime court records in Adriatic port cities, where she first encountered ledgers that contradicted official histories. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people who refuse to let institutions finish their sentences.

chapters.title: The Clock That Kept Two Times
chapters.summary: Ivo Marchetti, POV. Summoned to the observatory, Ivo finds the master clock running two minutes fast—deliberately—and a stranger, Lena Kovač, hiding among the gears with letters written by her supposedly dead father. She claims the clockmaker's guild was paid to slow time itself until a ship sails. Emotional beat: unease curdling into reluctant curiosity as Ivo recognizes his mother's name in one letter.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Lena POVs. In a candlelit workshop they authenticate the handwriting against guild records and reconstruct the stolen ledger's contents: debts, dowries, and inheritances erased when Lena's father 'drowned.' Enforcers begin asking questions at the guildhall. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose—Ivo realizes invisibility was always someone else's arrangement, never his choice.

chapters.title: What the Tide Carries Away
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, closing on Ivo. Racing through pre-dawn Trieste, they reach the harbor notary as the house's men burn the last original pages aboard the ship. A violent confrontation in the rigging; the master clock's escaped pendulum weight, repurposed as a counterweight, saves them but shatters the observatory clock below. Emotional beat: terror and clarity—the truth exists now only in their copies and their testimony.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At sunrise, the notarized copies enter the civic record just as the historians' ship slips past the mole; Lena stands on its deck, choosing to face her father rather than the archive. Ivo declines reinstatement, hanging a new compass above the guild door beside the repaired clock's remains. Emotional beat: quiet resolve—justice outside the law still leaves a mark on the record, and on the keeper.
